humaydi.bio: A Meccan jurist and leading pupil of Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah. Ibn Ḥajar reports his death in Mecca in 219 AH, with a later date also reported.
as: Trustworthy, a hadith master and jurist.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Al-Ḥumaydī is in our view an imam.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أثبت الناس في ابن عيينة الحميدي، وهو رئيس أصحاب ابن عيينة، وهو ثقة إمام
Al-Ḥumaydī is the most reliable of people on Ibn ʿUyaynah, the head of his students, trustworthy and an imam.
يعقوب بن سفيان, quoted by al-Mizzī
وما لقيت أنصح للإسلام وأهله منه
I have met no one more sincere towards Islam and its people than him.
He was trustworthy, with many hadiths.
He was trustworthy, with many hadiths.

t4324.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ al-ʿUmarī al-Madanī, Abū ʿUthmān, trustworthy and firmly established; Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ preferred him to Mālik in Nāfiʿ, and Ibn Maʿīn preferred him in al-Qāsim from ʿĀʾishah over al-Zuhrī from ʿUrwah; fifth generation; he died in the mid-140s; citing ʿ.
as: قدمه أحمد بن صالح على مالك في نافع
Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ preferred him to Mālik in [the transmission of] Nāfiʿ.
وقدمه بن معين في القاسم عن عائشة على الزهري عن عروة عنها
Ibn Maʿīn preferred him in [the chain of] al-Qāsim from ʿĀʾishah over al-Zuhrī from ʿUrwah from her.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أن مالكا في نافع أثبت من عبيد الله بن عمر
Ibn Mahdī held that Mālik is firmer than ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar in Nāfiʿ.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
فغضب وقال: هو أثبت من عبيد الله؟
Told that Ibn Mahdī rated Mālik firmer than ʿUbayd Allāh in Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān grew angry and said: Is he firmer than ʿUbayd Allāh?
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
عبيد الله أثبتهم وأحفظهم وأكثرهم رواية
Of Mālik, ʿUbayd Allāh and Ayyūb in Nāfiʿ, ʿUbayd Allāh is the firmest, best memoriser and most prolific.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
عبيد الله بن عمر من الثقات
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar is among the trustworthy.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Asked whether he preferred Mālik or ʿUbayd Allāh from Nāfiʿ, he said both and did not rank one above the other.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
عبيد الله بن عمر عن القاسم، عن عائشة: الذهب المشبك بالدر
ʿUbayd Allāh from al-Qāsim from ʿĀʾishah is gold set with pearls; he preferred it to al-Zuhrī from ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah.
أحمد بن صالح, quoted by al-Mizzī
عبيد الله بن عمر أحب إلي من مالك في حديث نافع
I prefer ʿUbayd Allāh to Mālik in the hadith of Nāfiʿ.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو بكر بن منجويه, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان من سادات أهل المدينة وأشراف قريش فضلا وعلما وعبادة وشرفا وحفظا وإتقانا
He was among the leaders of Medina and nobles of Quraysh in merit, knowledge, worship, nobility, memory and precision.
He was reliable, prolific in hadith, and an authority whose reports count as evidence.

t5518.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Qatāda ibn Diʿāma al-Sadūsī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb of Basra, as reliable and firmly established, head of the fourth generation, said to have been born blind, dying in the year 110s.
as: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما أتاني عراقي أحفظ من قتادة
No Iraqi with a stronger memory than Qatādah came to me.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
قتادة من أعلم أصحاب الحسن، ثم يونس بن عبيد
Qatādah was among the most learned of al-Ḥasan's pupils, followed by Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما كنت أظن أن الله خلق مثلك
I did not think God had created anyone like you (after Qatādah repeated back everything he had asked).
بكر بن عبد الله المزني, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت الذي هو أحفظ منه ولا أجدر أن يؤدي الحديث كما سمعه
I have not seen anyone with a better memory than him or more fit to convey hadith exactly as he heard it.
The dove that came out just as it went in is Qatādah; he has the best memory of all people.
كان قتادة إذا سمع الحديث يختطفه اختطافا
When Qatādah heard a hadith he would snatch it up at once.
ما زال قتادة متعلما حتى مات
Qatādah never stopped learning until he died.
لم يسمع قتادة من أبي العالية إلا ثلاثة أشياء
Qatādah heard only three things from Abū al-ʿĀliyah.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان قتادة أحفظ أهل البصرة لا يسمع شيئا إلا حفظه
Qatādah had the best memory of the people of Basra; he memorised whatever he heard.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Learned in Qur'an exegesis and in the disagreements of scholars.
عبد الرحمن ابن مهدي, quoted by al-Mizzī
قتادة أحفظ من خمسين مثل حميد
Qatādah has a better memory than fifty like Ḥumayd (al-Ṭawīl); Abū Ḥātim agreed.
Was there ever anyone in the world like Qatādah?
لا، بل قتادة، وما كان عند مكحول إلا شيء يسير
Asked whether Qatādah or Makḥūl was more learned: Qatādah; Makḥūl had only a little.
لم أر من هؤلاء أفقه من الزهري، وحماد، وقتادة
I saw none of them more learned in law than al-Zuhrī, Ḥammād and Qatādah.
I saw him; he is like a night wood-gatherer (taking knowledge indiscriminately).
أبو عمرو بن العلاء, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان قتادة، وعمرو بن شعيب لا يغث عليهما شيء يأخذان عن كل أحد
Qatādah and ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb rejected nothing as poor; they took from everyone.
حنظلة بن أبو سفيان, quoted by al-Mizzī
Qatādah was accused of Qadarite views.
وكان ثقة مأمونا حجة في الحديث. وكان يقول بشيء من القدر
He was reliable, trustworthy, and a hadith authority whose reports count as evidence. He held some views associated with Qadar.
ما كنت أظن أن الله خلق مثلك
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: I did not think God had created anyone like you (for memory).
كنت أعرف حديث قتادة ما سمع مما لم يسمع
I could tell Qatādah's directly heard hadith from what he had not heard, by his wording.
أعربوا الحديث فإن قتادة لم يكن يلحن
Read the hadith with correct grammar, for Qatādah made no grammatical errors.
عفان بن مسلم, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
كان قتادة يقيس على قول سعيد بن المسيب ثم يرويه عن سعيد بن المسيب. قال: وذاك قليل
Qatādah would reason by analogy from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab's view and then transmit it from him, though that was rare.
حماد بن سلمة, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
He hardly gave chains (until Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān came to Basra).
